{{Short description|Lithuanian-Brazilian mathematician (1963–2019)}}
'''Vladas Sidoravicius''' (1963, [[Vilnius]], [[Lithuania]] – 23 May 2019, [[Shanghai]]) was a Lithuanian-Brazilian mathematician, specializing in probability theory.<ref name=icmc>{{cite web|title=Vladas Sidoravicius (1963–2019)|date=17 August 2019|website=ICMC-USP, University of São Paulo|url=http://ebp23.icmc.usp.br/vladas.html}}</ref><ref name=impa>{{cite web|title=Mathematician Vladas Sidoravicius|website=Instituto de Matemática Pura e Aplicada (IMPA)|date=24 May 2019|url=https://impa.br/en_US/noticias/morre-o-matematico-vladas-sidoravicius/}}</ref><ref name=Shanghai>{{cite web|title=In Memoriam: Professor of Mathematics Vladas Sidoravicius, 1963–2019|date=29 May 2019|website=Shanghai NUY|url=https://shanghai.nyu.edu/news/memoriam-professor-mathematics-vladas-sidoravicius-1963-2019}}</ref>

==Education and career==
At [[Vilnius University]], Sidoravicius graduated in mathematics with [[Diplom]] in 1985 and [[Magister degree]] in 1986.<ref name=impa/> At [[Lomonosov State University]] he matriculated in 1986 and received his doctoral degree in 1990 with thesis advisor Vadim Aleksandrovich Malyshev.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=70459}}</ref> At [[Heidelberg University]] and at [[Paris Dauphine University]], Sidoravicius was a postdoc from 1991 to 1993.<ref name=impa/> In the early 1990s he gained an international reputation for his research in probability theory.<ref name=Shanghai/> In 1993 he moved to Brazil.<ref name=icmc/> He became a naturalized Brazilian citizen and was a full professor at the [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|Instituto de Matemática Pura e Aplicada]] ([[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|IMPA]]) in [[Rio de Janeiro]] from 1999 to 2015, when he moved to China.<ref name=impa/> At [[New York University Shanghai]] (NYU Shanghai), he was a professor of mathematics and also served as the deputy director of NYU Shanghai's NYU-ECNU (East China Normal University) Institute of Mathematical Sciences from 2015 until his death in 2019 at age 55.<ref name=Shanghai/>

Sidoravicius was the author or co-author of over 100 articles in refereed journals. He was a frequent collaborator of [[Harry Kesten]]. Their 2008 article ''A Shape Theory for the Spread of an Infection'' is particularly noteworthy.<ref name=Shanghai/><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v167-n3-p02.pdf|author=Kesten, H.|author2=Sidoravicius, V.|year=2008|title=A shape theorem for the spread of an infection|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=167|issue=3|pages=701–766|doi=10.4007/annals.2008.167.701|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 2014 Sidoravicius was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Seoul.<ref>{{cite book|author=Sidoravicius, Vladas|chapter=Criticality and Phase Transitions: five favorite pieces|title=Proceedings of the ICM, Seoul 2014|volume=4|pages=199–224}}</ref> In 2019 the XXIII ''Escola Brasileira de Probabilidade'' (XXIII Brazilian School of Probability) was dedicated to his memory.<ref>{{cite web|title=XXIII Brazilian School of Probability|date=17 August 2019|url=http://ebp23.icmc.usp.br/index.html}}</ref>
